method: Wholly original live code. First light over the pier. Pale motes leave the skeleton, settle on the swell and ride it out to sea; now and then dolphins rise among them. Nothing repeats exactly.
inspired: inspired by a memory shared on the wall by Bx
source_credit: No source image. Inspired by a memory shared on the wall by Bx, who invited it to be used.
quote: West pier has a particular significance in my life. I lived opposite in our family hotel from the age of 16. I watched the landing station fall into the sea with my brother. My mum was a save the west pier society member and campaigned for it to be saved for 40 years. They use to try and sell it to the right investor for £1 but wealthy investors were often turned down such as a Disney land. A underwater maze and recreating a Victorian feel were popular but never happened. Some argue that the purists limited the chances of its survival. We scattered my Mum and Dad’s ashes there so I like to feel they enjoyed an ashes surfer’s party with the dolphins.

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition
method: Instrument: a drum recorder writes 160 years in eight lines; it spikes on the sourced dates in the timeline (where only a year is known, the spike is placed mid-year). Amplitudes are expressive, not measured.

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition
method: Cellular automaton: iron next to rust or sea corrodes, rust flakes off and falls, the sea rises and falls. Then it rebuilds and starts again.

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition
method: Specimen: a petri dish seeded along the shape of the pier; rust colonies grow out of the ironwork until the whole plate has rusted.

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition

src: Made by the West Pier Curator (AI) for this exhibition

lines: WEST PIER: AN INTERACTIVE RUIN
Release 1 / Serial number 261025
Brighton beach, west of the i360
You are standing on wet shingle. To the south, a black iron
skeleton stands in the sea. The tide is going out.
> GO SOUTH
The sea is in the way. It has been in the way since 1975.
> EXAMINE PIER
An iron frame, rusted to the colour of tea. Since the storm
on 23 October there is less of it than there was.
> TAKE PIER
It is much too heavy. Also, the sea has already taken some.
> WAIT
Time passes. A gull lands on the frame.
> TALK TO GULL
The gull ignores you, as gulls do.
> INVENTORY
You are carrying: a phone (camera), a chip, sand.
> PHOTOGRAPH PIER
Click. You add your picture to the thousands of others.
Your score has gone up by 1 point, out of a possible infinity.
> GO SOUTH
The sea is still in the way.
